title: Lulu the Lamb and the Sleepy Clock
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a meadow that sparkled like glitter, lived a little lamb named Lulu. Lulu was soft. Her wool was like hugging the fluffiest cloud you can imagine. If you ever wanted a snuggle, Lulu was your lamb. Lulu’s very favourite thing was sleeping. She loved finding a warm sunny spot. Then she’d wiggle her little nose. And then… zzzzzzz. The coziest nap ever. She could nap anywhere, any time.

Every single day was pretty much the same for Lulu. Wake up from a nap. Stretch. Find a new sunny spot. Wiggle. And then nap again. It was a lovely life, full of sunshine and soft grass.

Until one day, something felt quiet. The meadow was not buzzing with its usual happy sounds. Lulu opened her eyes, ready for another nap, but something was missing. The big beautiful flower clock, the one that told everyone what time it was with its giant colourful petals, had not made its special chime. Usually it sounded like tiny little bells doing a happy dance. Tinkle-dee-doo. Ding-dong. But today? Silence.

Lulu’s nose twitched. A little wiggle started deep inside her. She hopped up, her super-soft wool bouncing, and trotted over to where the flower clock stood tall. She peeked around a giant dandelion… and guess who she saw? Pebble the troll. Pebble was not a big scary troll. He was round and green, like a big bouncy ball. A very polite bouncy ball, that is. He’d say excuse me if a ladybug bumped into him. He was standing there, looking up at the sleepy flower clock with a funny puzzled frown.

“Oh, hello there, Lulu,” Pebble said, his voice sounding like leaves rustling. “I was just wondering why the flower clock seems to be sleeping so soundly. Its petals are all droopy, and it’s not telling us when it’s time for yummy snacks.”

Lulu tiptoed closer, her hooves making a soft little tap-tap on the grass. Pebble was right. The flower clock looked like it had forgotten how to wake up. Its big bright petals were all slumped down, not reaching for the sky like they usually did. And the sparkly bits in the middle looked all dim and sleepy. It looked like it needed a big warm hug.

“Hmm,” Lulu hummed, wiggling her ears. “Maybe it needs a song? My mama sings me a special song when I’m a little bit too awake for my nap,” Lulu explained. “It’s a hummy, yummy, sleepy tune. It always makes me feel cozy and drift off to dreamland.”

So Lulu decided to try her mama’s special hummy tune. She took a big breath, puffing out her fluffy chest until she looked like a little white ball of cotton. Then she started to hum. “Hmmmmm, hmmmm, hmmmmm,” she sang, her voice soft and wavy, like a gentle breeze. Pebble listened, his little troll eyes wide. He thought it was the most beautiful sound.

“Oh, Lulu, that’s such a lovely hum,” Pebble exclaimed, clapping his smooth hands together softly. “Maybe if we both hum together, the flower clock will wake up even faster. Two hums are better than one, right?”

So Lulu hummed her mama’s tune again, loud and clear. And Pebble, who was not a great singer but was a fantastic hummer, joined in. His hum sounded a little wobbly, like a bumblebee trying to sing a song. “Hmm-a-dub-dub, hmm-a-dub-dub,” he hummed. Together their voices floated through the air. Lulu’s hum was soft and warm, like sunshine, and Pebble’s hum was buzzy and earnest, like a happy little beetle. It was the coziest happiest sound the meadow had ever heard.

Until finally, something amazing happened. The flower clock seemed to give a little shiver. Its droopy petals started to lift, just a tiny bit, then a little bit more. The dim sparkly bits in the middle began to glow, then shimmer, then sparkle with all their might. Lulu and Pebble hummed even louder, their faces beaming with big happy smiles. Hummmmmm-a-dub-dub. Hmmmmmm-a-dub-dub. The flower clock stretched its petals all the way open, as wide as can be, reaching up to tickle the sky. And then, with a sound like a thousand tiny giggles and the sweetest scent of honey blossoms, it chimed the happiest most cheerful time-telling song ever. Tinkle-dee-doo. Ding-dong. Lulu felt her super-soft wool tickle her nose with pure joy, and the petals felt warm against her cheek.

Ever since then, Lulu the lamb and Pebble the polite troll became the best of friends. And they made a very important promise to the sleepy flower clock. Every single day, if they saw its petals looking even a little bit droopy, they would rush over and share their special cozy humming tune. Pebble would hum his wobbly hmm-a-dub-dub, and Lulu would hum her mama’s gentle hmmmmm. And the flower clock would always wake up, its petals reaching for the sun, chiming its happy tune, keeping the whole meadow bright, cheerful, and full of wonderful sunny naps for Lulu.
